2_Introduction: The PSCs demonstrated a champion PCE of 23.606%, with a VOC of 1.1761 V, JSC of 25.351 mA/cm², and FF of 79.1751%. 1.65 mol/L Cs0.05MA0.1FA0.85PbI3.0 perovskite precursors were prepared. The film was deposited under controlled conditions, involving an initial spin of 1000 rpm (5 s) followed by a second spin at 5500 rpm (30 s). The crystallization process was refined by injecting 150 µL of antisolvent at last 15 s during spin-coating. Then the films were annealed at 110 °C for 15 min to form the perovskite layer.
3_Result_Discussion: The optimized crystallization of the Cs0.05MA0.1FA0.85PbI3 perovskite, facilitated by a rationally engineered sequential deposition process, begins with a high-concentration precursor (1.65 mol/L) that promotes a high nucleation density, while the tailored A-site cation mixture (Cs/MA/FA) optimizes the tolerance factor to enhance phase stability and suppress ion migration. The spin-coating protocol—an initial spread at 1000 rpm followed by a high-speed spin at 5500 rpm—ensures excellent solution thinning and uniformity, with the precise injection of 150 µL of antisolvent at the final 15 seconds inducing a controlled supersaturation state that governs the nucleation kinetics and favors the growth of larger, more oriented grains. Subsequent thermal annealing at 110 °C for 15 minutes then drives off residual solvent, facilitates Ostwald ripening for improved grain boundary connectivity, and effectively reduces bulk and surface defect densities, thereby minimizing non-radiative recombination centers and enhancing charge carrier lifetimes. This synergistic control over composition and crystallization dynamics directly results in superior photovoltaic parameters, yielding a champion device with a VOC of 1.1761 V, a JSC of 25.351 mA/cm², an FF of 79.1751%, and a PCE of 23.606%.
